No package.json — so we build a plain HTML app. Best approach: single-page canvas game with vanilla JS modules, no build step. Rich visuals via Canvas 2D (or maybe WebGL?). A lane-based auto-battler with animal/monster fusion mechanics.

Let me design the game deeply:

**Concept: "CHIMERA FRONT"** — a 5-lane tactical auto-battler where you splice creatures into units.

Core loop:
- You have a roster of base creatures (animals/monsters), each with attributes/traits.
- Splice two creatures into a hybrid: stats averaged + bonus, traits combined, possibly new named hybrid (e.g., "Wolf" + "Serpent" = "Wyrmhound").
- Place up to 5 units in 5 lanes (one per lane) vs enemy wave.
- Battle runs automatically in real time with lane combat: units march toward each other, attack, use abilities, projectiles.
- Win a wave → earn essence → splice more / upgrade units / heal.
- 5 waves per run? or endless with escalating waves. Add boss at wave 5, 10.

Tactical depth: lane assignment matters, unit classes (Tank, Striker, Ranged, Support, Bruiser), trait synergies, positioning rows (front/back)? 5 lanes, each lane has your unit and enemy unit. Units advance in lane and fight. Maybe each lane has 2 slots? Keep it simple but tactical:

- 5 lanes × 1 creature each, plus a "back line" support? Could do 2 rows: FRONT and BACK per lane. That's 10 slots. Might be too much. Let's do 5 lanes each with a front unit, and a shared "relay" bench allowing swapping mid-battle? Hmm.

Better design: 5 lanes, each lane you can place one unit. Enemy too. Units auto-battle in their lane; if a unit wins its lane, it pushes toward enemy core and damages nexus. Flanking rule: units that win lane move sideways to help adjacent lane? That adds tactical depth.

Alternative more tactical: Each unit has a lane position and a "range"; backline ranged units can shoot into adjacent lanes. Let's have 5 lanes with 2 deployment rows for the player: front row (melee) and back row (ranged). 10 slots total. During battle, melee advance in-lane, ranged stay back and shoot in-lane + adjacent lanes. That's genuinely tactical and visually rich.

Splicing:
- Creatures: Wolf, Bear, Falcon, Serpent, Scorpion, Toad, Rhino, Lynx, Shark? Fantasy: Dragon, Golem? "animals or monsters" — make a pool of animals + monsters.
- Each has base stats: HP, ATK, SPD (attack interval), RANGE, and traits (keywords like Frenzy, Venom, Guard, Regen, Frost, Burn, Flurry, Execute, Taunt, Leech).
- Splicing two creatures: you pick two from roster; result stats = weighted avg*1.15 + splice bonus, HP inherits more from bulkier parent, traits union (max 2 or 3), visual = procedural chimera combining heads/body/wings features. Name generated from parts (e.g., "Ironhide Direwolf"). The visual is the fun part: draw creatures procedurally with parts.

Procedural creature art: canvas 2D drawing with body shapes based on species parts. Spliced units combine parts: head type from one, body/wings from other, colors blended. This is achievable and can look cool with layered vector shapes, glowing eyes, shadows. Need to make it look polished, not cheap.

Let me plan visuals:
- Dark fantasy arena: deep navy/indigo background, mist, glowing rune lanes, torches. Top-down-ish 3/4 view arena with 5 lanes perspective? Simpler: side/plan view with lanes as horizontal strips? Classic lane battle: horizontal lanes going right (enemy on right). Camera side view. Units on each lane, walking right. 5 horizontal lanes stacked vertically. Field ~ 1000x600. Player units left, enemy right. Health bars above.

Better visual: isometric-ish flat arena with 5 lanes drawn as perspective trapezoids converging? Could be pretty: an arena viewed from above with slight perspective, lanes vertical strips going from bottom (player) to top (enemy). Units drawn as sprite-ish top-down-ish front-facing creatures. Actually front-facing creatures seen in 3/4 view lined up in 5 vertical columns (lanes) — classic "lane defense" look. Units advance up toward enemy. Their art can be front-facing chibi monsters — easier to draw expressive: body, head, eyes, wings, horns.

I'll do vertical lanes: 5 columns, each lane has a "front" and "back" slot? With vertical lanes, front slot is closer to enemy. Deployment: during PREP phase, click a unit from bench then click a slot. 5 lanes × 2 rows = 10 slots. Battle: units collide along lane; melee front units advance to meet enemies; ranged back units stay and shoot. That's tactically rich: putting a tank in front & archer behind in same lane.

Hmm, but combat then is mostly determined by numbers. Traits and lane targeting add tactics. Also add "Focus" abilities with cooldowns that player triggers? "tactical" could include active abilities: each unit has an ultimate you can trigger by clicking it once charged. That gives player agency during battle. Good idea: auto-battle + player-triggered abilities (each unit charges a meter; click unit or press 1-5 to cast). Provide "Rally" global ability maybe.

Scope control: I have to deliver a polished complete playable game. Let's define:

**Game flow**
1. Title screen → "Start Run".
2. Run structure: 6 waves? Each wave: PREP phase (deploy/splice, buy units), then BATTLE.
3. Currency: Essence earned per wave + interest? Keep simple: earn per win, spend on new base creatures (draft from 3 random) or heal/upgrade. Splicing is free but consumes both units? Careful — splicing consumes two roster units into one, which could reduce unit count. That's the core "mix" mechanic: roster size vs quality. Let's make splice consume both parents and produce one hybrid, with a bonus (stats + inherits traits, maybe +1 level). Units keep in roster; deploy up to 10 but roster limited to ~8? Hmm.

Simpler model that keeps it fun:
- You start with 4 base creatures. You can splice any two roster creatures into one hybrid (consumes both) — frees roster space and creates superior unit with combined traits. Merge also increases "Tier" (max tier 3 / up to 3 traits). Bench roster hold up to 6 creatures.
- Between waves, shop offers 3 random creatures for essence (cost scales). Also "Essence" reward each wave.
- Deploy: place roster units into 10 slots (5 lanes × front/back), any number up to roster size. Units persist wounds? Heal between waves fully to avoid complexity? Slight heal, plus shop upgrade. Let's fully heal each wave to keep it about composition — with difficulty ramp.

**Wave design**: 8 waves, each with enemy lineup shown (lane preview) so player can counter-deploy tactically. Enemy comps generated with increasing tier, boss at wave 4 and 8. Between waves you see next enemy lineup in prep; you can reposition. This makes "tactical 5 lane battle" real.

**Combat model**
Each unit: hp, maxHp, atk, atkInterval, range (melee ~ 60, ranged ~ 220), moveSpeed, traits, ability, energy.
Lane geometry: lanes x centers; vertical y from player base (bottom, y=big) to enemy base (top, y=small).
Rows: front row at y=0.62 field, back row y=0.82 (player), enemy front y=0.38, back y=0.18.

Simplify combat: units only interact within own lane, except ranged units can target adjacent lanes (priority own lane). Melee advances toward nearest enemy in lane until in range. Ranged stays behind front unit in lane, shoots nearest enemy in own or adjacent lanes. If lane empty, melee/ranged advance toward enemy nexus and attack it for big damage (lane break). Enemy nexus HP 100 shared; if lane breaks, unit attacks nexus each second for e.g. 12 damage. Player nexus similarly. Battle ends when a nexus reaches 0 or timer (45s) expires → side with higher nexus HP wins? Or remaining total HP ratio. Add sudden death after timeout.

Player abilities: each unit builds energy by attacking; at 100%, portrait glows; press 1-5/click to cast signature ability depending on dominant species (e.g., Bear → Shockwave stun; Serpent → Venom nova poison; Falcon → dive strike; Dragon → flame breath). Hybrids inherit ability of primary parent but buffed by secondary trait. Nice.

Traits:
- Frenzy: +25% attack speed below 50% HP
- Venom: attacks apply poison (stacking)
- Guard: reduces damage taken 20%
- Regen: heals 2% max HP/s
- Frost: attacks slow target
- Burn: attacks ignite
- Leech: heals 25% of damage dealt
- Flurry: 25% chance double strike
- Thorns: reflect 20% melee damage
- Swift: +20% move speed
- Execute: +50% damage to targets below 30%
- Taunt? not needed
- Splash: attacks hit adjacent lane? that's strong for a trait
- Aegis: shield at start
- Rally: nearby lane allies +10% atk

Keep ~10 traits.

Species pool (10-12):
1. Wolf — Striker, fast, Frenzy; ability: Howl (team atk buff)
2. Bear — Tank, high HP, Guard; ability: Shockwave (stun lane)
3. Falcon — Ranged, fast, Swift; ability: Dive (big single hit)
4. Serpent — Ranged/poison, Venom; ability: Venom Nova
5. Scorpion — Striker, poison/armor pierce, Thorns? ability: Sting (execute)
6. Toad — Ranged? Tanky support, Regen; ability: Mending Croak (heal team)
7. Rhino — Tank, charge, Thorns; ability: Charge (knockback+stun)
8. Lynx — melee dps, Flurry; ability: Pounce
9. Drake — Ranged, Burn; ability: Flame Breath (line damage)
10. Golem — Tank, Aegis; ability: Fortify (shield ally)
11. Wraith — Ranged, Leech; ability: Drain
12. Mantis — Striker, Execute; ability: Reap

Monsters + animals. Good.

Hybrid naming: prefix from one parent + base noun from other, e.g., "Frostfang" combos. We can build names by combining species name parts: Wolf→"Wolf", Bear→"Bear"... Hybrid: `${prefix} ${noun}` where prefix list based on trait/species: e.g., "Dire Wolfbear"? Let's do a name generator: take first parent's "epithet" (e.g., Wolf → "Grim", Bear → "Ironhide", Drake → "Ember") + second's noun ("Wolf", "Bear", "Drake") → "Grim Drake". For third splice: "Elder Grim Drake" etc. Also add tier suffix. Actually more evocative: "Emberhide Wyrm"? Let me store per species: noun (Wolf, Bear...) and adjective (Lupine, Ursine, Draconic...). Hybrid name = adjective of primary + noun of secondary, e.g., "Ursine Wolf". Then attach tier honorific: Tier2 "Elder", Tier3 "Ancient". Hmm "Ursine Wolf" sounds fine but dry. Use prefix names: "Ironmane", "Emberwing", "Venomfang". I'll create generated names via combining syllable sets keyed to species:
Wolf: "Fang", "Howl", "Grim"
Bear: "Iron", "Grav", "Ursa"
Falcon: "Sky", "Talon", "Aero"
Serpent: "Venom", "Coil", "Naga"
Scorpion: "Sting", "Barb", "Arakh"
Toad: "Mire", "Croak", "Bog"
Rhino: "Gore", "Tusk", "Bastion"
Lynx: "Shadow", "Pounce", "Nyx"
Drake: "Ember", "Pyre", "Draco"
Golem: "Stone", "Rune", "Terra"
Wraith: "Wraith", "Void", "Dusk"
Mantis: "Reap", "Blade", "Scythe"

Hybrid name = prefixA + suffixB where suffix can be species noun-ish "fang", "claw", "horn", "wing", "coil", "shell": e.g., "Emberfang", "Ironwing", "Venomhorn". Tier3 prefix "Elder"/"Ancient". This is fun. Unique names per pair can be generated deterministically.

Visuals: Procedural creature renderer. Each species contributes visual features:
- body shape archetype: quadruped (wolf, bear, rhino, lynx), serpentine (serpent, drake? worm), avian (falcon), insect (scorpion, mantis), amphibian (toad), humanoid/golem (golem), ghost (wraith).
- Combining two archetypes: use primary body archetype, add secondary's extra features (wings, horns, tail, extra eyes, armor plates) + tinted secondary color accents.

Design drawing in a 3/4 top-down-ish front view: Show creature from front: head, body behind, legs, arms/wings, tail. Drawing front-facing creatures procedurally is doable with rounded shapes, gradients, glowing eyes. Each species: color palette, horns/wings/spikes flags, eye count, head shape, body size, patterns (stripes/spots/scales).

I'll create a `creatureArt.js` that draws with canvas at given x,y,scale,facing. Use layered shapes + gradients + shadows + outlines. Add subtle idle bob and attack lunge animations, plus hit flash.

Arena aesthetics: 
- Background: deep teal/navy with vignette, distant mountain silhouettes / arena walls with banners, floating dust motes, god rays.
- Lanes: glowing stone paths, 5 vertical lanes separated by runes. Player base at bottom (nexus crystal), enemy at top.
- UI: HUD with essence, wave, nexus health bars top; bench strip at bottom with unit cards; shop drawer; splice modal; start battle button; speed toggle; log.
- Typography: use Google font? Network may be restricted. Better self-contained: use system fonts with strong styling (e.g., 'Cinzel' fallback serif for titles, 'Inter' ui). Could embed fonts? no. Use `Georgia, serif` for fantasy titles and system sans for UI. Maybe try loading Google font with fallback — offline capture may fail, but fallback handles it. I'll avoid external deps entirely to be safe (also app must work offline).

Layout: Full-screen game 1280×800-ish responsive. Arena center, bench bottom, right sidebar with wave/enemy info, splice panel. Must work at 1280 wide capture and typical screens. Use CSS grid: left arena canvas flexible, right panel 320px. Bench along bottom inside main.

Interaction:
- Prep phase: click bench unit to select → click a slot to deploy. Drag & drop also (nice but complex; click is fine, maybe implement drag too). Click deployed unit to pick up → click slot to move or "Recall" button.
- Splice: click "Splice" button opens modal with two parent selections from bench; preview shows resulting hybrid with stats/traits/art. Confirm. Splice costs essence? Maybe free but consumes both; limit one splice per wave to make it a decision. Or cost 4 essence. Let's make splicing cost essence ("Splice cost 6"), and free reroll? Hmm. Need to balance.

Economy:
- Start: 4 units (Wolf, Bear, Falcon, Serpent), 10 essence.
- Wave rewards: win = 8 + wave*2 essence; loss = run ends (roguelike). Nessus HP: if player nexus destroyed → defeat, restart run. Unit deaths in battle: units revive after battle (roguelike friendly) but you lose... maybe permadeath adds stakes but frustrating with splicing. Let's have units survive but nexus damage persists? Nexus heals 20 each wave. Keep simple: units always survive; defeat only if nexus destroyed.
- Shop: 3 offers, cost 5-8 essence; reroll 2. Roster cap 7; splice reduces count.
- Also "Upgrade" a unit for 4 essence: +12% stats? That competes with splice. Maybe skip; splicing covers growth.
- Between waves: +1 free random creature every 2 waves? With 8 waves and roster cap 7, splicing matters.

Waves: 8 with escalating. Show enemy lineup in right panel during prep with miniature cards and lane positions. Enemy units defined per wave with tier scaling.

Combat resolution details:
- Coordinate system in arena units (e.g., 0..1000 x 0..1000). Lanes at x = 100 + i*200 (5 lanes), field y: player nexus at y=960, enemy at y=40. Rows: player front y=620, back y=790; enemy front y=380, back y=210. Hmm units need to advance; melee will move toward enemy and stop when within range.
- Each unit has `y` (position) and `lane`, `side`, `row`. Ranged units in back hold ~position unless enemy enters range; if lane broken they advance.
- Target selection: nearest enemy in same lane; ranged can target adjacent lane at 0.65 damage? Actually allows cross-lane support. Let's say ranged prefer same-lane target within range; else nearest adjacent-lane target within range, at 100% (that's the tactical value of ranged). Melee only same lane.
- Movement: if no target in range in lane (and no adjacent target in range for ranged), advance toward enemy base at speed. Melee block: units stop when within range of target. To avoid units passing through each other, use simple y-collision: cannot move past enemy front by more than melee range.
- Damage: atk damage per hit, interval seconds. Apply traits.
- Energy: gain 12 per attack, 8 when hit; ability at 100; auto-cast? Player-triggered (press keys). If not triggered, units auto-cast at 100 after 3 seconds? To keep the game flowing if player is passive, auto-cast after charge completes (say 2s delay) — but manual gives timing advantage (e.g., heal when low). I'll allow manual cast anytime charged, and auto-cast after 4s. Communicate in tutorial tooltip.
- Battle ends when nexus HP 0 or timer 60s → compare nexus HP; tie → higher total remaining HP fraction wins.

Nexus attack: a broken lane unit advances to nexus and deals damage every 1.5s based on atk; takes some nexus retaliation? no. Nexus HP 120; damage per hit ~ max(6, atk*0.5)? With tier scaling, waves must be balanced. Alternative: nexus HP shared 100, lane break unit deals 8/s, so one lane break = 12s to win. Battles ~30s. Two lanes break = fast. Good.

Wave design: early waves 2-3 enemies so player can outnumber; later 6-8.

Need enemy abilities too? Simplify: enemies use same simulation and can cast abilities automatically. Fine.

Battle log / floating damage numbers, hit sparks, death fade, screen shake, lane glow. Sound: WebAudio synth for hits, casts, UI, victory/defeat. Include mute toggle. That adds a lot of polish. Implement simple synthesized audio (no assets).

Persistence: localStorage for best wave / runs? Maybe just "best wave" and settings. Add pause? Not needed.

Screens:
- Title with animated background (arena + creatures) and "BEGIN THE RITE" button, brief instructions.
- Run (prep/battle).
- Victory/defeat summary modal with restart.
- Codex/modals: splice modal, shop modal? Make shop inline in right panel with offers.

I need to be careful with scope but deliver high quality. Let's structure files:

- index.html
- styles.css
- src/main.js (app/bootstrap, state)
- src/data.js (species, traits, names, waves)
- src/art.js (creature drawing + arena drawing effects)

- fill gradient; distant arches; floor with rune-lit lanes; glowing lane dividers; nexus crystals at ends with pulsing glow; fog particles; embers.
- 5 lanes as corridors with slight perspective widening toward bottom maybe. Keep straight vertical for gameplay clarity; add decorative side rails.
- Each slot marked with a circular rune plate (deployment slots), highlighted during prep, showing assigned unit silhouettes.

- Enemy units under a subtle red rim; player under cyan rim.
- Floating damage numbers, poison ticks, heal sparkles, projectile arcs, melee slash arcs, impact bursts.

- Use unit.art computed from species pair: bodyType, palette (primary color, secondary), features (horns, wings, spikes, tail, mane, eyes, plates, glow).

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url

  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown

  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button

  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

# OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review. Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests. ## Wiki index - [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md) - [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md) - [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md) - [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md) - [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md) - [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md) ## Main project file The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml). Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md) aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job. Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue. Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run. ## Shell timing When writing shell scripts, always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands. Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command; the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in interactive shell commands. ## Ideas Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under `./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as `ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`. ## Links in handoffs When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use the `codex://threads/` URL format. When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days. ## OpenCode GitHub Actions To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user. Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation. The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session, verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward. When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status. Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ` for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`, which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit. Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account. Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only. Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota. Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound. Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries. Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save. Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker. To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with `gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`, then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ` to discover the host and port and SSH with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper. When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when live log evidence can be collected. For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper: ```sh bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ``` The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from `_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while inspecting the runner. ## Mac SSH access The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as: ```sh ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p runner@.agentsweb.space ``` The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running. ## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`: ```sh bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub ``` For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and use the same key: ```sh ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \ -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \ -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \ -p runner@.agentsweb.space ``` Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never print secrets while inspecting a worker. ---

One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? --- github-actions-visual-workflow-editor.md github-agent-project-comparison.md ios-builder-native-app-generation.md issue-triggered-opencode-workflow.md live-source-file-browser.md omgithub-self-hosted-supabase-migration.md opencode-docker-sandbox.md opencode-oauth-env-auth.md opencode-token-isolation.md remix-preview-port-ownership.md

function findTarget(b, u){
  const candidates = alive enemies;
  let best=null, score=Infinity;
  for (e of candidates) {
    const dy = Math.abs(e.y-u.y); const dx = Math.abs(e.x-u.x);
    const sameLane = e.lane===u.lane;
    if (!sameLane) {
      if (u.range < 150) continue;
      if (Math.abs(e.lane-u.lane)>1) continue;
    }
    const dist = Math.hypot(dx,dy);
    if (dist > u.range + 15) continue;
    let s = dist + (sameLane?0:120);
    if (s<score){score=s;best=e;}
  }
  return best;
}

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable lane-based tactical fighting game where players splice animals/monsters into unique chimeras and battle across 5 lanes, as a browser app in `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround`.

## Requirements
- Build now without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly at the end.
- Save small JPEG screenshots (`.jpg` paths, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; use PNG only for fine detail.
- No external runtime dependencies preferred; static HTML app served via default runtime.

## Decisions
- Vanilla ES modules + Canvas 2D + CSS, no build step, self-hosted fonts (`assets/fonts/`).
- Game named **CHIMERA FRONT**; 8 authored waves + endless mode; 5 lanes × 2 rows (front/back); up to 8 roster units.
- Splice mechanic: first parent = primary form/range/ability; second contributes traits/colors/stats; tier max 4 ("Mythic"); splices consume both parents.
- Economy: start 14 essence, shop recruits (cost `5 + ceil(wave/2)`), reroll 2, splice cost `4 + tierA + tierB`.
- Abilities charge automatically; player can click/press 1–8 to cast early; auto-cast after 6s.
- Procedural creature art for 12 species and hybrid feature combinations; synthesized WebAudio SFX.
- Battle sim is pure/logic-separated; HUD/UI in `main.js`; renderer/effects in `scene.js`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Core data for 12 species, 13 traits, 12 abilities, 8 waves, endless wave generator (`src/data.js`).
- Unit factories, hybrid stat/trait/name/art derivation (`src/units.js`).
- Full battle simulation with lane movement, targeting, ranged adjacent-lane support, traits, abilities, nexus damage, bloodrush, events (`src/battle.js`).
- Procedural creature renderer with 9 body archetypes plus cross-lineage features (`src/art.js`).
- Arena/title renderer with lanes, nexus gates, braziers, particles, projectiles, ability FX, health/energy bars (`src/scene.js`).
- Complete app UI: title, prep/battle sidebars, roster dock, shop, splice modal, help, results, toasts, tooltips, keyboard controls, persistence of best wave (`src/main.js`).
- Full styling and responsive layout (`styles.css`), `index.html`, audio (`src/audio.js`).
- Server running on port 3002 via tmux session `chimera`; title and initial prep screens load successfully.
- Fixed a runtime crash (`enemyRow` was reading `wd.enemies` objects instead of `S.enemyPreview`); game now reaches prep screen with zero console errors.

- Visual polish/testing: just captured `/screenshots/art.jpg` from temporary `art-test.html` to evaluate all creature art, but have not viewed it yet.

"your creatures match from left to right to oppose the enemy's creatures" = your creatures in each row line up left-to-right against enemy creatures in the same row.

Question: Does "match from left to right" mean lane 0 (top) = enemy's leftmost? Standard auto-battler: player rows on left, enemy rows on right, each row fights horizontally. So we need to rotate the battlefield 90°: 5 horizontal lanes (rows), player on left, enemy on right. Each lane has front/back columns? That would be player's "front" closer to center (right side of player area) and "back" further left; enemy front closer to center (left side of enemy area), enemy back further right.

This is a significant coordinate change: all battle logic uses y-position for advance, x=Lane_x. Need to swap x/y semantics or remap. Let's think about minimal change:

Current battle logic probably moves along y (advance) and lanes differ by x. To make horizontal, we can transpose coordinates: lane axis = y, advance axis = x. Need to change all movement/targeting/distance logic. That's substantial but doable with a coordinate abstraction.

Alternative: keep battle logic unchanged, but rotate the rendering 90°? That would make text bars rotated, no.

Better: rewrite coordinate mapping in battle.js:
- Lanes become horizontal rows: lane y positions.
- START_X: player front/back on left, enemy front/back on right.
- Advance direction: player moves +x (right); enemy moves -x (left).
- Units' lane is still lane index 0..4, row front/back.
- distance uses both x and y. Targeting likely uses same lane primarily; ranged support adjacent lanes uses y adjacency maybe. Need inspect battle.js thoroughly.

Maybe simpler: use a global transform helper `pos(u)` where world x = f(advance), y = g(lane). If battle logic uses only u.x/u.y and distance/movement along "advance", we can swap definitions:

- But existing code uses x for lane (LANE_X[lane]) and y for advance. Could redefine makeCombatUnit: x = advance coordinate, y = lane row. Then all uses of u.y as position along lanes, and u.x as cross-lane. We must update wherever movement happens.

Let me grep battle.js for x/y usage patterns.

However target distances remain computed in sim space (both axes), which affects ranged support etc. That's fine because sim remains consistent; only visual mapping is transpose. import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
const runtime = join(process.env.HOME, '.local/share/omgithub-playwright')
const require = createRequire(join(runtime, 'package.json'))
const { chromium } = require('playwright')
const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(runtime, 'linux.json'), 'utf8'))
process.env.DISPLAY ||= ':' + readFileSync(join(runtime, 'display'), 'utf8').trim()
const browser = await chromium.launch(config.browser.launchOptions)
const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1280, height: 800 } })
page.setDefaultTimeout(15000)
const errors = []
page.on('pageerror', e => { errors.push(e.message); console.log('PAGEERROR', e.message) })
page.on('console', m => { if (m.type() === 'error') { errors.push(m.text()); console.log('CONSOLE', m.text()) } })
await page.goto('http://localhost:3002', { waitUntil: 'load' })
await page.waitForFunction(() => document.fonts.status === 'loaded')
await page.waitForTimeout(500)
const shot = async (name) => { await page.screenshot({ path: `screenshots/${name}.jpg`, type: 'jpeg', quality: 85 }) }
